question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, CFO Kress explicitly said gross margins will bottom in Q4 FY27 in the 71-72% range (memory cost inflation), recovering to 72-73% in FY28 as price increases take effect. Q3 guide is 74.0% ±50bp GAAP=non-GAAP; Q2 actual 75.0%. NVIDIA's formal guides usually land near prior explicit commentary, so midpoint ~71.5%. Downside skew: memory prices 'exceeded expectations and headed higher'; GAAP can sit 0.1-0.2pt below non-GAAP. Upside: conservative pre-guide, earlier pricing actions. No human market on the Q4 guide; Polymarket Q3 actual adjusted GM markets (73-75% at 0.85, low volume) are a near-miss consistent with the Q3 guide.
calls.dossier:
- NVIDIA Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026): Q2 GAAP and non-GAAP GM both 75.0% (flat q/q; 72.4-72.5% a year earlier). Q3 FY27 outlook: GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% ±50bp; revenue $108.0B ±2%; GAAP opex ~$9.2B.
- Q2 FY27 earnings call (Aug 26, 2026; Motley Fool transcript): CFO Kress: 'We expect margins to bottom in Q4 in the 71% to 72% range before settling at 72% to 73% in fiscal year '28', as price increases take effect in Q1 FY28. Memory: 'magnitude of the price increase has exceeded our prior expectations and are headed even higher into next year.' Kress: 'We want to be direct about this rather than let it linger as an open question.'
- Earlier commentary (FY26 calls/search summaries): management had targeted 'mid-70s' GM for FY27; Q1 FY27 guide was GAAP 74.9% / non-GAAP 75.0% ±50bp. So the 71-72% Q4 trough is a downward revision from that target.
- GAAP vs non-GAAP GM gap: recent quarters 0.0-0.2pt (Q3 FY26 actual 73.4% GAAP vs 73.6% non-GAAP; Q1 FY27 guide 74.9 vs 75.0; Q3 FY27 guide equal at 74.0).
- Historical precedent: NVIDIA's one-quarter-ahead margin previews have generally been close to the later formal guide (e.g., 'exit FY26 in mid-70s' -> Q4 FY26 guide 74.8% GAAP / 75.0% non-GAAP).
- October 2026 analyst commentary (TIKR and others) repeats the 71-72% Q4 trough and 72-73% FY28 path; bear view: recovery depends on pricing power, which custom silicon threatens.
- Status quo: the Q4 guide matches the stated 71-72% trough (midpoint 71.5%). Upside: conservative guide or earlier price increases. Downside: memory costs keep rising, Rubin ramp mix/yields, GAAP-only charges.
- Resolution: resolves off the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (GAAP GM midpoint, rounded to 0.1%), not the non-GAAP figure or call commentary. Release expected Nov 17, 2026.
- Event window: single release on Nov 17, 2026; as of Oct 27, 2026 no release yet (about 3 weeks remain).
- Searched for but could not find: any NVIDIA margin update between Aug 26 and Oct 27, 2026 (conferences, 8-Ks), or any prediction market on the Q4 guide itself (only Polymarket markets on the Q3 actual adjusted GM).

calls.reconciliation: All three runs found the same facts: the Q2 FY27 call guided to a Q4 trough of 71-72%, the Q3 guide is 74.0% +/-50bp with GAAP equal to non-GAAP, there was no intra-quarter update, and no market prices the Q4 guide. There were no factual disputes. The only judgment differences were minor tail widths (1.2-1.4) and whether to price escape mass. I kept median 71.5 and a 1.2 width, with small symmetric escape mass for a shock outside the 68.95-73.05 range. I had no web access on this run and retrieved nothing new.

disagreements.claim: Width of the tails (90-10 of 1.2 vs 1.4)
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks the tie. Took 1.2 because the explicit pre-signal is tight and NVIDIA's history of matching pre-signals supports it.

disagreements.claim: Whether to declare escape mass beyond the bounds
disagreements.verdict: Declared ~1% each side for tail shocks (memory-cost shock or unusual GAAP charges below; a pricing regime change above).
